name: C++ Interview Questions and Answers
title: C++ Interview Questions and Answers
description: Revise all the important concepts of C++ and prepare yourself for the interviews. Check explanation of the questions if you are not able to solve them and learn new concepts.

modules.name: Basic C++ Syntax and Concepts
modules.description: The fundamental building blocks of C++ programming. Includes core language elements and structures used to write C++ code.

modules.name: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Basics
modules.description: A programming paradigm based on the concept of "objects" containing data and code. It focuses on creating reusable and modular code through classes and objects.

modules.name: Memory Management
modules.description: The process of allocating, using, and freeing memory in C++ programs. Involves understanding how memory is organized and handled during program execution.

modules.name: Exception Handling
modules.description: A mechanism for dealing with runtime errors or exceptional situations in programs. Allows for graceful error handling and recovery in C++ applications.

modules.name: File I/O
modules.description: Input/Output operations for reading from and writing to files in C++. Enables programs to interact with external data stored in files on the computer.

modules.name: Pointers and References
modules.description: Variables that store memory addresses, allowing direct memory manipulation. Essential for dynamic memory allocation and efficient data handling in C++.

modules.name: Standard Template Library (STL)
modules.description: A collection of powerful, reusable components in C++. Provides efficient implementations of commonly used data structures and algorithms.

modules.name: Const Correctness
modules.description: A principle in C++ for using the 'const' keyword to prevent unintended modifications. Helps in writing more robust and error-free code.

modules.name: Virtual Functions and Abstract Classes
modules.description: Mechanisms for achieving runtime polymorphism in C++. Allows for creating interfaces and implementing method overriding in derived classes.

modules.name: Templates
modules.description: A feature that allows writing generic, type-independent code in C++. Enables creating flexible functions and classes that work with different data types.

modules.name: Operator Overloading
modules.description: The ability to redefine the behavior of operators for user-defined types. Allows custom types to behave like built-in types in expressions.

modules.name: Namespaces
modules.description: A feature to organize code into logical groups and prevent name collisions. Helps in managing large codebases and avoiding naming conflicts in C++.
